curated-gf-original-surfer-gf-sura: Original Surfer swells and snaps from fat curves to wire-thin ends. Sura, a serif, keeps its own contrast low and its terminals open, so the headline gets all the drama while the text underneath stays dignified.
curated-gf-over-the-rainbow-gf-armata: Over the Rainbow looks like a thin rod bent into letters. Armata, the sans-serif partner, spaces its characters generously and fills the line height, which gives the loose handwriting a sturdy, modern anchor to lean on.
curated-gf-overlock-gf-fira-code: Fira Code, a monospace, leaves clear channels of blank space between its letters. Overlock's chunky, nearly touching rounds sit above it, say, on a stack overflow style Q&A, though the body isn't meant for long paragraphs.
curated-gf-overlock-sc-gf-heebo: Overlock SC stands out with its broad, open counters and barely any height gap between cases. Heebo is a plain sans with a tall central band, so if the text feels dense, enlarge it a notch.
curated-gf-oxanium-gf-noto-sans-thai-loo: Noto Sans Thai Looped has tall bodies that make its lowercase look bold (say, for personal trainer branding). Oxanium is best at flat, single-weight linework with curves ending in clear daylight, while the sans below does its best work with generous gaps at curve ends.
curated-gf-pangolin-fs-trench-slab: Trench Slab, a serif, sits low and dignified, with little step between its lowercase and capitals. And Pangolin's friendly one-nib handwriting, with its unthinned curves and wide c openings, is where the pair gets its charm, best enjoyed in small doses.
curated-gf-paprika-gf-lexend-peta: Lexend Peta, a sans, reads with a big x-height and wide-mouthed curves. Paprika's scattered, capital-like lowercase would suit, say, a travel vlog title, but shrink the heading and its big personality gets lost.
curated-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-zanabaza: Paprika scatters its letters apart, and its lowercase fills the line like capitals. Noto Sans Zanabazar Square, a plain sans, answers with a soaring x-height and wide gaps that keep tiny sizes crisp, which is the pair's real strength.
curated-gf-parisienne-gf-radley: Radley, with open counters and sturdy downstrokes, would look at home on a pottery studio sign. Parisienne's closed, nearly fused letters and oversized capitals are what make the pair memorable, while Radley lets the eye move freely.
curated-gf-passero-one-gf-geist-mono: Expressive and bold, Passero One huddles its letters together with narrow e channels. Geist Mono, a monospace, suits a regex cheat sheet, though enlarging it too much would crowd out the heading's punch.
